strengths: Well-structured presentation progressing from problem motivation to theoretical analysis to practical solution.
Comprehensive empirical validation across multiple datasets.
The paper is well motivated and studies an important problem from an interesting perspective
The paper is generally well written and easy to follow
The problem tackled is important and this paper approaches it through the concept of Dirichlet energy.
The method seems to offer empirical enhancements on various benchmarks.
The paper proposed a very intuitive and generally applicable idea to effectively alleviate the over-smoothing problem for GNNs.
The proposed idea is well-motivated by solid theoretical insights and results.
The paper is easy to read.
The authors revealed that the Dirichlet energy decay in deep GNNs is linearly proportional to the edge space sum with a constant $c$.

The authors provided that, within the Dirichlet energy analytic framework, it is crucial for the activation function $\phi$ to satisfy $\phi(0)=0$ in Proposition 3.2. This may indirectly explains why adding a shift $b$ in SReLU is effective.
The minimum Dirichlet energy constrained message updating scheme showed a good performance.
weaknesses: Limited Novelty: using Dirichlet energy to overcome oversmoothness has been extensively studied.
lack of detailed analysis of computational overhead compared to baseline methods

The proposed method has limited novelty given existing works that have explored similar ideas and model designs, e.g., [1,2]. Adding self-loop or residual link or strengthening the information of the centered nodes have been extensively used by existing GNN models, such as the well-known ones [1, 2]

The theoretical results are not new and have been derived in the literature, e.g., [3, 4]. The result of Lemma 1 has been proved in [3] and [4]. Besides, the analysis presented in this paper only shows the result that is already well-known, i.e., over-smoothing will happen when the layer increases. There lacks analysis in why and how the propose model can address the over-smoothing.

The experimental evaluation is limited in small datasets and comparison with state-of-the-arts is insufficient. More experiments on large datasets such as ogbn-products and ogbn-proteins are suggested. More comparison with state-of-the-art GNNs, especially the ones that can overcome over-smoothing, e.g., GCNII, are needed.

Though a lot of efforts have been paid on discussing Dirichlet energy, how the proposed approach is linked to preserving Dirichlet energy still remains very unclear. Eq. (8) was introduced alone while more theoretical investigations and experimental observations should be incorporated.

The presentation needs improvement. Wordy sentences present at times with many of them constantly repeated, e.g., the contents in Sec. 4.1 has been discussed multiple times in the previous sections and should be simplified for more informative contents.

Some concepts were introduced with confusion and did not exhibit strong correlation to the proposed approach. For instance, how Proposition 3.2 is related to Eq. (8) (e.g., how Eq. (8) help address the vanishing problem) is unclear. There is also no clear reason of introducing the edge space (Definition 3.2) and Corollary 3.1 conveys limited information.

Experiment settings are not convincing. For example, the reported performance of the baselines are remarkably lower than the official leaderboard of obgn-arxiv (https://ogb.stanford.edu/docs/leader_nodeprop/#ogbn-arxiv).
Misuse of citet vs citep in multiple places hinders the readability. The authors are encouraged to correct these presentation issues.
Some theoretical terms in Section 3 are not sufficiently introduced and explained. The authors are suggested to provide more detailed background and solid definition of the quantities involved.

Several parts are repetitive or even inconsistent. For example, Section 4.1 is redundant and repetitive of the earlier content, as well as the Hyperparameter Analysis with its three following paragraphs in Section 5.2.
The hyperparameter analysis is not insightful. The study of different activation functions, hidden dimensions, and dropout rates is old-fashioned and not unique to the proposed approach.

Lack of novelty: This paper is a direct follow-up of [1]. The authors revealed that the Dirichlet energy decay in deep GNNs is linearly proportional to the edge space sum with a constant c, and that the activation function must satisfy φ(0)=0. The proposed update functions are remarkably similar to those in [1] except for a weight matrix. The main contribution is stated as choosing the initial Dirichlet energy as a lower bound, but the authors need to clarify how their method distinguishes itself from or enhances the previous approach and elaborate on the significance of omitting the weight matrix.

Lack of experiment: Dirichlet energy visualization. Plotting the Dirichlet energy of each layer with and without the $E_{init}$ term would be more persuasive. As stated in Section 4.2, 'The initial Dirichlet energy serves as a lower bound for the Dirichlet energy,' it is expected that $E_{Dirichlet}$ will converge to the lower bound $E_{init}$ as the number of layers increases.

Lack of experiment: The claim that $E_{init}$ preventing topological collapse in Section 4.2 should be supported by experimental evidence. Visualizing the node representations in the final layer and comparing them to the initial topology would be helpful. Consider using commonly employed techniques, such as t-SNE visualization[2][3] or a color-propagation test[4].
